items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 3, 2026
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Tuesday, including Americans heading to polls on Tuesday in midterm elections, US military carrying out “defensive” strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island, and Belgium’s prime minister submitting his resignation to King Philippe amid a budget deadlock. Americans head to the polls Tuesday in midterm elections that will decide control of Congress and shape President Donald Trump’s ability to advance his agenda during his final two years in office. More than 54 million people have already voted early. Republicans are defending narrow majorities in both chambers, with rising prices and the war on Iran weighing on the party’s standing. Winning the House would allow Democrats to block legislation and launch investigations into the administration. Taking the Senate would also give them the power to reject Trump’s nominees, including federal judges. The first polls close at 6 p.m. Eastern, with results arriving throughout the night. Close contests could leave control of one or both chambers unresolved beyond election night. - US carries out 'defensive' strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island: Report The US military carried out "defensive" strikes against Iran’s Qeshm Island, local media reported, citing a US official. "This was a defensive measure for Iranians using surface to air missiles against US assets," the official was quoted as saying. The attack, which was first reported by The Wall Street Journal, comes as President Donald Trump has sought to downplay the prospect of a renewed large-scale military confrontation with Iran following Tuesday’s midterm elections. However, US officials told the Journal that American forces have continued conducting smaller-scale strikes against Iranian targets for several weeks. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Monday that it downed two US drones south of Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. - Belgian prime minister offers resignation amid budget deadlock Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever submitted his resignation to King Philippe after his five-party coalition failed to agree on the 2027 budget, but the monarch deferred a decision and announced consultations with coalition leaders. "The King is holding his decision in suspense and will begin consultations with the presidents of the majority parties tomorrow," the Royal Palace said in a statement posted on the US social media platform X. De Wever met the monarch at the Royal Palace in Brussels for more than 90 minutes amid tensions over efforts to address a €10 billion ($11 billion) budget shortfall, according to public broadcaster VRT. Negotiations have been deadlocked for weeks, with disagreements reportedly centered on the Flemish socialist Vooruit party and the Francophone center-right Reformist Movement (MR).

items.excerpt: Author: Associated Press Published: 12:00 AM EST November 3, 2026 Updated: 12:04 AM EST November 3, 2026 Supreme Court rejects Trump administration push to set aside thousands of California ballots WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court on Monday rejected the Trump administration’s push to force California to set aside thousands of ballots from people the federal government claims are noncitizens, a decision that came hours before the final day of voting in the pivotal midterm elections. The high court refused to immediately intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state’s voter rolls. The swift rejection capped a string of losses for the president’s effort to intervene in the election before the counting of ballots to decide who controls Congress in the last two years of his second term. No justices publicly dissented. “The Court rejected Trump’s emergency request without even asking the other side to respond,” California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, posted on X. “Democracy won.” Several lower courts also rejected the Justice Department's push to set aside the challenged California ballots until the voters’ citizenship status could be verified. And in a case that revolved around the future certification of Alaska's election results, a judge did not even hold a hearing before dismissing a Trump-ordered suit to prevent a possible Democratic Senate win. Parts of a Learjet may have broken off midair before Florida crash that killed 9, investigators say WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — A business jet that crashed in Florida and killed all nine people aboard, including a family with two young children, likely started breaking apart before it slammed into the ground and erupted in a fireball, a federal investigator said Monday. The jet did a steep nosedive, leaving behind a crater and a wide debris field as rain pounded the area. Authorities said weather will be a key initial focus of the investigation, and that the National Transportation Safety Board will also examine the actions of the crew and look for any mechanical problems with the plane. The plane burst into flames when it crashed in Greenacres, about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site and little remained of the plane. The victims included the 20-year-old co-pilot, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, who made the final radio transmissions, as well as technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife, Helen Sharp, and their two young children, relatives said. About 600 nearby residents remain displaced, but only one injury was reported on the ground. ... Rain clears but flood risk remains high after destructive storms swamp normally arid US Southwest The skies were clearing, but the risk of flooding remained over parts of the U.S. Southwest after powerful downpours sent massive amounts of water surging over the usually dry landscape, forcing hundreds to evacuate and keeping swift-water rescue teams busy. Officials said cleanup and repair efforts could take weeks. One person died in the floodwaters and police suspect a second death was weather-related. The National Weather Service said Monday that isolated cloudbursts were still possible across the Four Corners region — where New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado and Utah meet — as the phenomenon stoked by warming Pacific waters known as El Niño disrupts weather patterns. ... Russia bombs aid center and shelter in southern Ukraine, killing 26, officials say KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia bombed an aid distribution center and neighboring shelter in southern Ukraine on Monday, killing 26 people, Ukrainian officials said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a post on X that strikes first targeted a school building used to distribute humanitarian aid and then took aim at a nearby shelter. “This is further proof that Russia wants no de-escalation,” Zelenskyy said. The attacks in the village of Komyshuvakha, in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, occurred as a limited ceasefire expired Monday in Kherson, a different region in the country's south. The limited ceasefire agreement had allowed humanitarian aid and evacuation missions into front-line areas in Russian-occupied territory. “There was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible,” Zelenskyy said. “With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings.”

items.title: Oil prices climb after U.S. reportedly strikes Iran's Qeshm Island
items.excerpt: Published Tue, Nov 3 2026 1:41 AM EST Updated An Hour Ago Lim Hui Jie@in/hui-jie-lim-a7371176/ - Brent crude was up 0.97% on Tuesday at $105.77 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate was up 0.97% to $97.41. - The rebound in oil prices come a day after the U.S. and Iranian presidents signalled they are open to a diplomatic solution to Iran war. - Washington attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal, adding that the U.S. has been carrying out "limited strikes" against the country in recent weeks. ... Oil prices climbed on Tuesday after the U.S. reportedly struck Iran's Qeshm Island late Monday, one day before the midterm elections. Brent crude Add To Watchlist was up 1.75% on Tuesday at $106.60 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate Add To Watchlist was up 1.7% to $98.10. Oil prices rebounded a day after the U.S. and Iranian presidents signaled they are open to a diplomatic solution to the Iran war, which saw oil prices sell off over 7% on Monday. But before this development, Brent prices were at their highest since 2022, as fears of further U.S. strikes on Iran after the midterms mounted. Washington attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal, adding that the U.S. has been carrying out "limited strikes" against the country in recent weeks. The military campaign against Iran has been kept deliberately low-profile to avoid signaling plans for a major escalation in fighting, the report said, quoting an unnamed official. But despite these strikes, the Trump administration has also been touting a possible diplomatic solution to the conflict, with Vice President JD Vance telling CNN, "The president and I both feel really good about the prospect of potentially coming to a negotiated settlement." On Sunday, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump would like to resolve the Iranian war "diplomatically," and prefers not to use military force. High oil prices have contributed substantially to inflation and high gasoline prices in the U.S., which have become a cause of concern for Trump ahead of the midterm elections. Last week, two Federal Reserve presidents said interest rates will need to move higher to rein in inflation. Higher rates generally crimp growth and raise costs for consumers, but help to bring down inflation.

items.title: El Niño could push US inflation up by 1 percentage point, Fed research warns - The Herald Business
items.excerpt: Published : Nov. 3, 2026 - 14:24:34 San Francisco Fed analyzes weather's impact on prices El Niño estimated to have lifted PCE inflation 0.3 percentage points from April to July La Niña follow-up next year could push prices up by as much as 1 percentage point Climate risk compounds oil and tariff pressures on Fed El Niño El Niño could push US inflation up by as much as 1 percentage point next year, according to new Federal Reserve research — adding a climate wildcard to an already fraught inflation outlook shaped by rising oil prices and tariff increases. The findings present a fresh complication for the Fed, which has maintained a restrictive monetary policy stance in its effort to bring prices under control. The San Francisco Federal Reserve Bank said in a recent edition of its Economic Letter research publication that El Niño poses a significant risk of driving up US prices in 2027, Reuters reported Monday (local time). El Niño is a weather pattern in which sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific rise above normal levels, triggering droughts, floods and extreme heat in various parts of the world. The World Meteorological Organization warned last month that the current El Niño episode could be among the most powerful on record, with droughts expected in some regions and flooding in others, driving up temperatures and extreme weather events globally. Three San Francisco Fed researchers wrote in the report that they estimate the current El Niño may have raised the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index by about 0.3 percentage points between April and July this year. They added that while the initial inflationary effect is expected to fade by the end of this year, prices could rise by as much as 1 percentage point in 2027. That projection, however, assumes that this year's El Niño is followed by a La Niña event next year. La Niña is the opposite phenomenon — sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific fall below normal — and, like El Niño, affects climate patterns and agricultural production around the world. The researchers also flagged the risk that extreme weather could interact with existing supply chain vulnerabilities. "Recent developments — including disruptions in fertilizer markets, supply chain bottlenecks in energy markets and record-breaking weather events — could interact with the current El Niño in unexpected ways," they said. Should extreme weather disrupt agricultural production and logistics, it could add further upward pressure on food prices and energy costs. The findings come as US inflation has remained above the Fed's target for an extended period. The Fed has been contending with a succession of price shocks: supply chain disruptions during the COVID-19 pandemic, a sharp round of tariff increases last year, and rising international oil prices this year. US inflation has now exceeded the Fed's 2 percent target for more than five and a half years. Growing demand for AI-related goods and services has also been cited as a new source of upward price pressure. With financial conditions assessed as not particularly restrictive, the Fed faces mounting pressure to keep inflation in check. The Fed held its benchmark interest rate steady last week, but markets are pricing in the possibility of additional rate increases in December and next year to rein in inflation. Meanwhile, the researchers found that El Niño could also have a positive effect on US job growth even as it pushes prices higher. That divergence — with extreme weather affecting inflation and employment in opposite directions — could force the Fed into increasingly difficult trade-offs between its two policy mandates if El Niño's inflationary impact intensifies next year.

items.title: Movie News: 3rd November 2026
items.excerpt: # Movie News From Around the World ¦ 3rd November 2026. November 3, 2026 by bobwp ### Wicker’s UK number one, Clayface’s quiet global win, Jailer 2 breaks ₹800 crore, Marrakech’s line-up, the AFM, Iceman casting & Carrie turns 50. Morning, all. Yesterday I promised you the UK-Ireland chart and the Jailer 2 numbers, and they’ve both landed. Tuesday also means our weekly lap of the world’s other film industries, plus there’s a very special anniversary. UK and Ireland box office: Black Bear’s Wicker had the first number one film in its distributor’s history, opening to £1.7 million from 676 cinemas, a £2,515 average, which rises to £1.8 million including previews. A24’s Primetime, starring Robert Pattinson as To Catch a Predator‘s paedo-hunting host Chris Hansen, opened in third place with £1.3 million from 560 cinemas, a £2,321 average, and £1.7 million with previews. Clayface dropped 37% in its second weekend to £1.2 million, taking it to £4.7 million. It’s a Halloween weekend for the re-releases, too, with Pan’s Labyrinth in 384 cinemas, Donnie Darko in 202 and Ken Russell’s The Devils in 73 in a new 4K restoration from BFI Distribution. The weekend box office, worldwide: Clayface topped the worldwide chart for a second weekend with an estimated $22.8 million, which is dismally low for a chart-topping film, as a lack of significant new releases over Halloween weekend left the market becalmed. The UK and Ireland is its biggest international market, with $6.1 million to date. Laika’s astounding Wildwood moved up to second place after international expansion, and Wicker was seventh with a $7 million start, made up of $4.1 million from North America and $2.6 million from nine international markets. In the UK, Wicker‘s opening beat those of Poor Things and The Shape of Water, according to Deadline. Elsewhere, Resident Evil has now passed $400 million worldwide. In North America, yesterday’s estimates have been confirmed, and You Can See Everything came out on top with $11.4 million in its third weekend, a little higher than expected, ahead of Clayface with $11 million. Clayface now has $44.6 million in North America and $83 million worldwide, while the whole weekend came in at roughly $60 million, one of the slowest of the year. Tamil cinema: Jailer 2 breaks ₹800 crore: Rajinikanth’s Jailer 2 passed ₹800 crore worldwide on its 18th day, finishing its third weekend with a worldwide gross of ₹807.25 crore (about $84 million), according to Sacnilk. It’s the first Tamil film to pass both ₹700 crore and ₹800 crore, and it now stands as the highest-grossing Tamil film ever and reportedly the second-highest-grossing Indian film of 2026. It has earned ₹456.3 crore net in India (about $48 million) and ₹273.5 crore (about $28 million) overseas, and it added ₹26.4 crore net in India over its third weekend. The Far East: Resident Evil’s China hold: In mainland China, Resident Evil was number one for a fourth consecutive weekend with RMB 28.5 million ($4.3 million), taking it to $71.3 million since its 5 October opening. The crime drama Traces of Justice remains ahead overall with $98.5 million since 1 October. The wider market had a quiet weekend with $18.2 million, and the year-to-date total of $4.73 billion is down 29.0% on 2025. A 2014 re-release of John Wick opened in third place. Marrakech’s line-up: The 23rd Marrakech International Film Festival, which runs from 20 to 28 November, has unveiled a line-up of 76 films from 39 countries, including 10 world premieres. As I mentioned when it closed the London Film Festival, Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut opens the festival, and Marion Cotillard presides over the competition jury. Gala screenings include Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial and James Gray’s Paper Tiger, and 14 films compete for the Étoile d’Or, including Yoon Dan-bi’s The World Before and Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo’s Ben’imana. The American Film Market gets going: Hockey’s Hollywood moment, largely driven by the success of Heated Rivalry, has reached the AFM, with Liam Neeson set to play a legendary coach in Believe 13, about his bond with an injured high school star. Closer to home, Guy Pearce, Sabrina Impacciatore, Rachael Stirling and Selena Tan have joined Jeff Daniels in Trudie Styler’s The Reception, a chaotic wedding-party comedy that’s currently shooting on location in Scotland. Iceman casting: Ben Wang, the star of Karate Kid: Legends, who also plays District 12 tribute Wyatt Callow in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping on 20 November, is in talks to play Iceman in Marvel’s X-Men reboot, which Jake Schreier is directing for 2028. The deal isn’t done, and Gabriel LaBelle, Jackson Kelly and Rhenzy Feliz all reportedly tested for the part. It would leave Beast as the only member of the original team without an actor, and the casting news arrives just days after Patrick Stewart’s farewell as Professor X was confirmed. Fifty years of Carrie: Cheering things up, Brian De Palma’s Stephen King adaptation opened in the US 50 years ago today, on 3 November 1976, in 17 cinemas. Sissy Spacek, who was 26 when she played the bullied teenager, and Piper Laurie, as her fanatically religious mother, were both nominated for Oscars, and it was Laurie’s second nomination after The Hustler. It was the first film adapted from a King novel, made on a budget of $1.8 million, and it grossed $33.8 million. Prom night has never been the same since.
